title: How Many Taps
trend: TikTok 'How many taps until my pet gets mad' (owners count gentle head taps until the pet reacts; ppl.studio TikTok formats, Proven, November 2026, US) — teen Nia films herself counting taps on the family bunny Sir Reginald, who narrates his calm, while Grandpa Earl brags he is the most patient man on the street; twist: one tap from the bunny and Grandpa explodes, and Reginald reveals he has tapped Grandpa's bald head every night at three in the morning for two years while Grandpa blamed a leak in the roof
youtube_title: How many taps until the bunny gets mad? Grandpa wanted a turn 🐰
description:
Nia wants to know how many taps it takes to make Sir Reginald mad. Grandpa Earl says patience runs in the family. Sir Reginald has been keeping count too.

#cartoon #animation #funny #bunny #shorts
tiktok_caption: how many taps until the bunny gets mad? grandpa wanted a turn 🐰 #cartoon #animation #funny #bunny

lines.text: Okay. How many taps until my bunny gets mad? Let's find out.
Tap one.
Good evening. I am Sir Reginald. I have been tapped before.
Tap two. Tap three.
I am a rabbit. I am at peace. I am a small fluffy lake.
Tap four. Tap five. Nothing. Not even an ear.
The ears move for carrots only. That is the arrangement.
What are you doing to that rabbit?
Science, Grandpa. How many taps until he gets mad.
In my day we did not tap animals. We tapped maple trees.
I make no syrup. Please do not get ideas.
Tap ten. Tap eleven. Tap twelve.
Twelve. A dozen. Like eggs. I know about eggs. Seasonal work.
He will never get mad. He gets it from me.
Grandpa, you yelled at the toaster this morning.
The toaster knew what it did.
It made toast. That is all it has ever done.
Tap twenty. Tap twenty one. Still nothing.
Let me try. Patience recognizes patience.
Tap. Tap. Tap.
His tap is very heavy. Like being knighted by a sandwich.
See? Calm. He respects me.
I respect the hand. The hand has a cookie in it.
That is my cookie.
It was.
Tap fifty. This is my longest video ever.
Some of us were born calm, Nia. Thirty years at the post office.
May I try something?
Wait. You want a turn?
One tap. On the grandpa.
Go ahead. Nothing gets to me.
Oh no.
Tap.
Hey! Who taps a man on the head? Who does that? In my own house!
One tap. One. Grandpa got mad in one tap.
One tap. That is all it takes for a grandpa. I have tested this.
Tested it? When?
Every night. Three in the morning. For two years.
That was you?
One tap. You say, who is there. I hop away.
I called a man about the roof. I thought it was a leak!
Grandpa paid a man four hundred dollars to look at a dry roof.
Lovely man. I watched him from the window. Very thorough.
Why? Why would you do this?
You took my spot on the couch two years ago. I remember everything.
So he is not patient. He is just waiting.
Rabbits do not get mad. Rabbits get even.
Okay. Okay. You can have the couch spot.
And the cookies.
And the cookies.
And Thursday nights. I watch the cooking show.
Fine! Fine. Thursday is yours.
This is the best video I have ever made.
Next one. How many taps until Grandpa gets mad.
One.
Zero, actually. I checked. He is mad right now.
I am not mad. I am just loud.
Goodnight, Earl. See you at three.
